Collected in 666 settings, including schools, colleges, and skilled nursing facilities, this dataset enabled direct comparison of within-setting transmission to community-wide risk. Elevated transmission was concentrated in specific age-defined subpopulations-older adolescents in schools, undergraduates in colleges, and residents in nursing facilities-with little additional risk among other groups, notably including staff. Young adults, particularly in colleges, played a disproportionate role in spread, and new viral lineages consistently expanded first within this group. Viral spread followed reproducible urban-to-rural gradients, and vaccination was associated with reduced onward transmission. We further estimated sequencing thresholds required for timely detection of emerging variants. Together, these findings reveal consistent demographic and spatial structure in SARS-CoV-2 transmission that can inform viral respiratory pathogen genomic surveillance.

items.abstract: Highlights from the Science family of journals.

items.abstract: Editors' selections from the current scientific literature.

items.title: Quantum-classical separation in bounded-resource tasks arising from measurement contextuality.
items.abstract: Quantum phenomena can be exploited to tackle certain problems beyond the reach of classical approaches. In this study, we focus on coordinated decision-making among many players without communication, the study of which, on current quantum processors, has remained elusive. Using a superconducting qubit processor, we show that quantum contextuality enables certain tasks to be performed with success probabilities beyond classical limits. With a few qubits, we illustrate quantum contextuality with the magic square game and quantify it through a Bell-Kochen-Specker inequality violation. To examine many-body contextuality, we implement the N-player Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger game and separately solve a two-dimensional hidden linear function problem, advancing the state of the art on fidelity and system size in both tasks. Our work introduces benchmarking of quantum processors using contextuality-based algorithms.

items.title: Balancing redox-mediated cytotoxicity and catalysis in natural product biosynthesis.
items.abstract: Redox-mediated chemistry is central to both the biosynthesis and cytotoxicity of many natural products, yet how microbes balance these processes remains poorly understood. Here, we uncover a conserved mechanism that coordinates three redox-mediated processes in secondary metabolite biosynthesis: self-protection, prevention of substrate degradation, and late-stage biosynthesis. Using the antitumor antibiotic doxorubicin as a model system, we show that the vicinal oxygen chelate (VOC) protein DnrV prevents reactive oxygen species formation and substrate degradation while promoting P450 catalysis. We expand this paradigm to a conserved family of VOC-fold proteins, redox-associated cytotoxin-binding proteins (REACT), found across bacteria, fungi, and plants. REACT represents a multifunctional protein class that balances antibiotic assembly, self-protection, and prevention of metabolite destruction, providing a foundational understanding of production of redox-active natural products.

items.title: Meso-microporous zeolitic materials with thin walls containing ordered 10-ring channels.
items.abstract: Aluminosilicate zeolites offer exceptional size and shape selectivity but suffer from diffusion limitations imposed by subnanometer micropores. Intrinsically meso-microporous zeolites integrate mesopores with micropores to create interconnected pathways that accelerate diffusion while preserving selectivity, yet their synthesis remains challenging. In this study, we report NJU120-5 and NJU120-7, intrinsically meso-microporous aluminosilicates that integrate micropores with mesopores enclosed by two-T-atom-thick walls containing 10-ring channels, forming a fully interconnected three-dimensional pore network. Their plausible framework models were established on the basis of advanced electron ptychographic imaging, revealing representative quasi-rectangular mesopores in calcined NJU120-5 with a uniform width of ~12 angstroms and lengths from 41 to 162 angstroms. Both materials exhibit high porosity, strong Brønsted acidity, and enhanced performance in heavy-oil cracking, delivering high yields of valuable fuels with suppressed coke formation.

items.title: Bumble bee cognition.
items.abstract: Bees provide clues about the origins of intelligence.

items.title: Digital doubles and the modern crisis of identity.
items.abstract: Our vulnerabilities are features, not flaws, that unite us-and set us apart from our data-based avatars.

items.title: A neural code for generative speech production in human Wernicke's area.
items.abstract: Wernicke's area in the posterior temporal lobe is classically defined by its role in speech comprehension, yet a paradox remains: Why does damage here also profoundly impair speech production? Using direct human brain recordings, cortical stimulation, and lesion analysis, we found that this region is not solely for perception. A discrete subzone within Wernicke's area, the left posterior superior temporal gyrus (lpSTG), becomes active before speech, is causally necessary for speech production, and codes features of whole upcoming words rather than low-level acoustics or articulatory information. Its neural activity is distinct from the auditory-feedback responses nearby and can decode intended speech in people with paralysis. Thus, while Wernicke's area is a key part of auditory cortex, it contains a dedicated subregion for speech generation.

items.title: A thalamo-amygdalar circuit drives female vulnerability to chronic pain after early-life stress.
items.abstract: Childhood adversity increases the risk of chronic pain and anxiety later in life, particularly in women, yet the neural mechanisms linking early-life stress to adult vulnerability remain elusive. Here, we show that social isolation and nerve injury interact to amplify activity-dependent synaptic gain and anticipatory recruitment of the paraventricular thalamus-to-central amygdala pathway in female, but not male, mice. This female-specific circuit sensitization enhances mechanical hypersensitivity and avoidance behaviors in adulthood. Chemogenetic pathway inhibition selectively rescued these behaviors when stress and injury co-occurred, whereas sustained and phasic pathway activation triggered mechanical hypersensitivity and avoidance, respectively. Together, these findings uncovered a latent thalamo-amygdalar synaptic gain state that is unmasked by a subsequent injury and transforms early-life stress into female-specific vulnerability to chronic pain and anxiety-like avoidance.

items.title: Rising risk of deforestation in Indonesia's pulp sector.
items.abstract: Recent trends reverse progress toward zero-deforestation.

items.title: Interpenetrating bottlebrush elastomer for low-loss soft ultrasonic interfaces.
items.abstract: Ultrasound imaging relies on soft interfaces that transmit sound efficiently between a device and the body. Conventional gel couplants provide low acoustic loss but contain mobile liquid phases that can dry, flow, or leach during extended use. By contrast, mobile phase-free elastomers are more stable but generally attenuate megahertz ultrasound strongly, limiting their use as couplants. We report an interpenetrating bottlebrush elastomer molecularly designed to overcome this trade-off. A densely grafted backbone lowers the shear modulus without increasing shear loss, whereas well-packed sidechains reduce bulk compressibility, jointly suppressing acoustic attenuation in a soft elastomer. The resulting elastomer combines soft tissue-like mechanics with low-loss acoustics, providing a durable couplant for soft ultrasonic interfaces.

items.title: Telemetric calorimetry for wireless continuous reaction profiling.
items.abstract: Real-time monitoring of chemical reactions is often achieved with specialized instrumentation along with custom-designed reactors or intrusive sampling. In this study, we introduce reaction telemetry, a wireless analytical strategy that enables remote, nonintrusive monitoring directly within operating reaction vessels. This approach uses light-powered microelectronic devices that communicate optically and function as autonomous sensing elements. We demonstrate continuous calorimetric measurements across diverse chemical reactions relevant to pharmaceutical and fine chemical synthesis, including photochemical and electrochemical systems, providing access to reaction kinetics under native operating conditions with subsecond temporal resolution. The resulting measurements will support catalyst evaluation, safety assessment, and mechanistic investigation and will accelerate data-driven reaction discovery. By embedding analytical functionality directly within reaction vessels, reaction telemetry establishes a general framework for information-rich observation of chemical processes across research, development, and education.

items.title: Divergent activation of the RXFP1 relaxin receptor by protein and small-molecule agonists.
items.abstract: The relaxin receptor RXFP1 is a therapeutic target owing to its potential benefits in the treatment of fibrosis and heart failure. Protein and small-molecule agonists are currently in midstage clinical trials for various forms of heart disease. In this work, we present three cryo-electron microscopy structures of RXFP1: ligand-free, bound to the native agonist relaxin-2, and bound to the small-molecule drug candidate AZD5462. These structures reveal that relaxin-2 engages the receptor's ectodomain, whereas AZD5462 binds to the transmembrane domain. Together with hydrogen-deuterium exchange mass spectrometry, we show that relaxin-2 induces reorganization of the linker domain into a helical secondary structure. By contrast, AZD5462 stabilizes an active conformation through a distinct set of conformational rearrangements. Altogether, our findings define divergent activation mechanisms for protein and small-molecule agonists of RXFP1.

items.title: Atmospheric organic nitrogen is a major nutrient source to global oceans.
items.abstract: Atmospheric nitrogen (N) deposition is a critical nutrient source for marine ecosystems, but its organic nitrogen (ON) component remains poorly quantified. We measured ON in marine aerosols collected during 21 research cruises transecting multiple ocean basins and both hemispheric high latitudes. We used these observations to constrain and evaluate an atmospheric chemistry model with updated ON sources and sinks, enabling global mapping of ON deposition. The model estimated annual ON deposition to oceans at 12.8 (4.0 to 22.7) teragrams of nitrogen per year (Tg N year-1), contributing 27% (11 to 40%) of total N deposition. Marine emissions supply 3.9 (0.7 to 6.9) Tg N year-1 (30%) of deposited ON, while terrestrial sources contribute 8.9 (3.3 to 15.7) Tg N year-1 (70%). In N-limited regions such as the central Atlantic and Indonesian seas, ON accounts for ~50% of total N deposition.

items.title: Angular momentum transfer from an optical vortex to an atomic rotor.
items.abstract: Light carries angular momentum in two forms: spin, associated with polarization, and orbital, associated with helical wavefronts. Whereas spin angular momentum underlies well-known atomic selection rules, the role of orbital angular momentum (OAM) in light-matter interaction continues to be discussed in the literature. In this work, we investigate OAM transfer from a vortex laser beam to a trapped-ion quantum rotor using rotational sidebands of the electric quadrupole transition of 40Ca+. We directly observe coherent transfer of optical OAM into quantized rotation and identify distinct selection rules for different rotational sidebands. This observation provides experimental evidence for a scale-dependent separation of angular momentum transfer pathways in light-matter interactions. Further, our work elucidates the previously reported modified selection rules in trapped-ion experiments, establishing a unified framework for twisted light-matter interactions.

items.title: The fate of poised pre-mRNAs shapes mitochondrial activity and cellular differentiation.
items.abstract: Although RNA quality control tightly regulates gene expression, the scope of its regulatory functions in the nucleus remains unclear. In this study, we describe the quality control, on chromatin, of poised intron-containing polyadenylated RNAs (PIA-RNAs). Whether these precursor messenger RNAs (pre-mRNAs) constitute immature mRNAs whose splicing is pending or, alternatively, are degraded by the nuclear RNA exosome depends on whether they engage nuclear cap-binding protein 3 (NCBP3) or anillin, respectively. Many PIA-RNAs inversely controlled by NCBP3 and anillin encode mitochondrial factors. Thus, NCBP3 depletion in mouse as well as pathogenic mutations in the RNA exosome in humans result in reduced mitochondrial activity, muscle weakness, cerebellar hypomyelination, and diminished motor coordination. Our findings reveal a competition between pre-mRNA metabolic pathways whose balance controls mitochondrial function and, when perturbed, leads to neurological diseases.

items.title: Molecular adhesion for durable metal halide perovskite modules.
items.abstract: Reliable, strong, and low-loss interfaces are needed for durable perovskite photovoltaics. We have developed a molecular interface layer with an aromatic dual-site-binding ligand to improve the reliability of perovskite modules. The buried interface was strengthened through intermolecular interactions between the ligand and hole-selective layer and through strong chemical bonds. The resulting heterointerface enhances perovskite adhesion and releases interface strain, making the device more resilient to thermomechanical stresses. This device architecture achieves a power conversion efficiency of 22.7% for 900-square centimeter (cm2) submodules (aperture area: 655 cm2) and 21.3% for 7200-cm2 standard modules (aperture area: 6380 cm2). The champion 7200-cm2 standard module maintained consistent performance during 105 days of outdoor testing, as independently measured by the Photovoltaic Accelerator for Commercializing Technologies (PACT) center.

items.title: Quiet within, chaos without: Turbulence shelters drive selective particle capture and release.
items.abstract: Turbulence is chaotic, yet its fluctuations follow a structured, nonequilibrium energy cascade unconstrained by the equilibrium theorems that limit passive energy extraction from molecular gases. Here, we introduce turbulence shelters: hollow shells with a single aperture that filter eddies by scale, sustaining gradients in fluctuation intensity that drive directional particle transport despite zero mean fluid flux. Across three orders of magnitude in size, shelters establish particle concentration contrasts between their interior and the surrounding flow, with selectivity controlled by particle geometry, inertia, thermal fluctuations, and electrostatic forces. At the microscale, shelters discriminate particles differing by tens of nanometers independently of material composition. These results establish a design principle for selective filtration: Geometry that compartmentalizes turbulent fluctuations can harness ambient eddies to direct particle transport.

items.title: Elastic-field reorganization stabilizes soft-lattice perovskites for durable solar cells.
items.abstract: The soft lattice that enables the exceptional performance of halide perovskites inherently compromises their operational stability. Here, we show that soft-lattice perovskites can be stabilized through elastic-field reorganization induced by rigid nanodiamond inclusions. Their inclusion enabled efficient bulk-to-boundary load transfer, redistributing and dissipating internal elastic fields at grain boundaries rather than allowing their accumulation within the crystal interior. Suppression of intergranular sliding constrained lattice deformation and mitigated defect generation during prolonged operation. Devices based on the stabilized perovskites with an area of 0.09 square centimeters achieved a certified power conversion efficiency of 27.6%, and minimodules with an area of 16.1 square centimeters achieved 24.3%. These devices retained 80% of their initial PCE after 5000 hours of maximum power point operation at 85°C and 98% after 5000 hours of dynamically varying light-intensity day-night cycling.

items.title: Zero-shot de novo design of a metalloenzyme.
items.abstract: De novo design of enzymes is a frontier challenge, requiring consideration of catalytic mechanism and optimization across biochemical and biophysical criteria. Here, we present dEVA (design by EVolutionary Algorithm), a multi-objective protein design method built on principles drawn from evolutionary biology. We apply dEVA to the zero-shot, de novo design of metalloenzymes by optimizing the coordination sphere of catalytic metals. We characterize a bi-zinc metalloenzyme that exhibits promiscuous hydrolytic activity towards both phosphomonoesters and phosphodiesters. This design achieves a rate enhancement ((kcat/KM)/kw) of up to 3 x 1013 relative to the uncatalyzed reaction, comparable to characterized natural phosphatases. Structural characterization via x-ray crystallography and absorption spectroscopy supports the design of a de novo active site. These results demonstrate that de novo enzymes can be designed without pre-specified motifs, natural templates, or evolutionary information.

items.title: Quaternary carbon-guided carbocation cascade rearrangement to enantioenriched polycycles.
items.abstract: Polycyclic frameworks are prevalent in natural products and bioactive molecules, yet their efficient enantioselective synthesis remains a longstanding challenge. Carbocation cascade cyclization is a textbook reaction that has transformed the synthesis of fused polycycles, but extending this strategy to bridged architectures requires precise control over highly reactive carbocation intermediates while overcoming the intrinsic energetic barrier of transannular cyclization. Herein, we report a quaternary-carbon-guided carbocation cascade rearrangement platform that enables enantioselective and divergent assembly of complex polycyclic architectures from readily available substrates. An enantioenriched quaternary center, installed via transition-metal-catalyzed allylation, serves as a temporary structural linchpin in an acid-triggered cationic cascade rearrangement process, forming multiple bonds and chiral centers in a single step. In combination with pre-embedded quaternary centers, this strategy provides bicyclic and bridged polycyclic frameworks bearing multiple stereocenters with high enantioselectivity.

items.title: Widespread marine mammal and seabird reductions are unlikely to benefit salmon due to indirect ecosystem effects.
items.abstract: Pacific salmon are depleted due to anthropogenic impacts, and populations have failed to recover despite management interventions. Predation on salmon by pinnipeds and seabirds has been suggested as a barrier to recovery, leading to calls for predator culls by some. However, no studies have evaluated the whole-ecosystem impact of removing these predators nor estimated the direct and indirect effects of these culls on salmon. We use an end-to-end ecosystem model to assess the efficacy of widespread culls in marine environments. We find that culls are unlikely to benefit salmon due to the indirect food web effects of predator reduction and the low biomass of top predator groups. Instead, more abundant fish predators, northward-expanding competitors, and temperature-sensitive prey have larger effects on salmon in the ocean.

items.title: Assessing Multiple Treatment Regimens for Tuberculosis.

sections.objective: Ganfeborole and BTZ-043 are new drugs that may improve tuberculosis treatment.
sections.methods: In this phase 2, randomized, controlled trial, we assigned participants with rifampin-susceptible pulmonary tuberculosis to receive the standard four-drug combination (isoniazid-rifampin-pyrazinamide-ethambutol; HRZE) for 24 weeks; bedaquiline-delamanid-moxifloxacin for 16 weeks; or one of 10 new four-drug combinations for 16 weeks. The new regimens contained ganfeborole, BTZ-043, or both, with combinations of bedaquiline, delamanid, moxifloxacin, pyrazinamide, pretomanid, and linezolid. The primary end point was the log10(time to positivity) slope (rate of change from baseline to week 12 in the time to Mycobacterium tuberculosis growth in a positive sputum culture). The treatment effect was assessed as the Bayesian posterior probability of superiority of each new regimen to HRZE with respect to the primary end point (results were used to select regimens for further evaluation, rather than for characterization of efficacy).
sections.results: A total of 401 participants underwent randomization; 371 were included in the modified intention-to-treat population and 400 in the safety population. We identified two promising regimens for further evaluation: ganfeborole-bedaquiline-pretomanid-moxifloxacin (BPMG) and BTZ-043-bedaquiline-delamanid-moxifloxacin (BDMT). The log10(time to positivity) slope was 0.129 log10(days) per week (95% Bayesian credible interval, 0.112 to 0.146) with BPMG and 0.142 log10(days) per week (95% Bayesian credible interval, 0.126 to 0.160) with BDMT, as compared with 0.118 log10(days) per week (95% Bayesian credible interval, 0.105 to 0.131) with HRZE, for a relative difference of 9.1% (95% Bayesian credible interval, -8.6 to 29.0) and 20.5% (95% Bayesian credible interval, 2.7 to 41.1), respectively, and a posterior probability of superiority of 0.83 and 0.99. The incidence of adverse events of grade 3 or higher was 38% in the BPMG group (none of the participants discontinued), 28% in the BDMT group (one discontinued because of a drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms), and 24% in the HRZE group (none discontinued). Bedaquiline-moxifloxacin-pyrazinamide-BTZ-043 was discontinued because of hepatotoxic effects.
sections.conclusion: In this trial, two four-drug regimens, one with ganfeborole and one with BTZ-043, showed evidence of potential efficacy and a safety profile that did not preclude progression to further evaluation. (Funded by Innovative Medicines Initiative 2 Joint Undertaking and others; PARADIGM4TB ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06114628.).

items.title: Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome.
items.abstract: Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) is a common cause of acute hypoxemic respiratory failure in patients with pneumonia, sepsis, aspiration of gastric contents, severe trauma, or other inciting triggers. Although the definition of the syndrome has evolved over the past several decades, the core elements (acute onset, hypoxemia, and bilateral radiographic opacities) remain consistent. Critical components of management include identification and treatment of the underlying cause of ARDS as well as avoidance of ventilator-induced lung injury and volume overload. Ongoing areas of controversy include the best strategy for supporting nonintubated patients, personalization of positive end-expiratory pressure, the role of innovative ventilatory strategies, and the use of glucocorticoids. New research suggests that precision medicine approaches to ARDS management that focus on discrete biologic, radiographic, or physiological subphenotypes may improve outcomes, and prospective trials of these approaches are ongoing.

items.title: Anbenitamab plus HB1801 for HER2-Positive Advanced Breast Cancer.

sections.objective: The combination of docetaxel, trastuzumab, and pertuzumab (THP) is an established first-line treatment for human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-positive advanced breast cancer. The efficacy and safety of anbenitamab, a HER2-targeted bispecific antibody, plus albumin-bound docetaxel (HB1801) in this context are unknown.
sections.methods: In this phase 3, multicenter, open-label, randomized trial conducted in China, we randomly assigned patients with HER2-positive advanced breast cancer in a 1:1 ratio to receive either anbenitamab plus HB1801 or THP. The primary end point was progression-free survival, as assessed by blinded independent central review. Objective response was a secondary end point.
sections.results: A total of 885 patients were enrolled (445 were assigned to receive anbenitamab plus HB1801 and 440 to receive THP). At this prespecified interim analysis (with 401 events [disease progression or death] and a median follow-up of 21.0 months), the estimated 24-month progression-free survival was significantly higher with anbenitamab plus HB1801 than with THP (58.5% vs. 34.4%; hazard ratio for progression or death, 0.46; 95% confidence interval, 0.37 to 0.56; P<0.001). The percentage of patients with an objective response was 87.6% in the anbenitamab group and 73.4% in the THP group. Adverse events of grade 3 or higher occurred in 204 of 444 patients (45.9%) in the anbenitamab group and in 151 of 439 patients (34.4%) in the THP group. Neutropenia was the most common adverse event of grade 3 or higher in both groups (13.1% in the anbenitamab group and 8.4% in the THP group). Adverse events leading to death occurred in 2 patients in each group.
sections.conclusion: Anbenitamab plus HB1801 led to significantly higher progression-free survival than THP among patients with HER2-positive advanced breast cancer. (Funded by Shanghai JMT-Bio Technology and others; HEALER ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05838066.).

items.title: Trial of Endovascular Therapy for Mild Stroke with Large-Vessel Occlusion.

sections.objective: Whether endovascular therapy benefits patients with mild acute ischemic stroke from large-vessel occlusion involving the anterior circulation is uncertain.
sections.methods: We conducted a multicenter, open-label, randomized trial in China involving patients with acute ischemic stroke of mild clinical severity (defined by a score of <6 on the National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale) that had resulted from large-vessel occlusion involving the anterior circulation. Patients also had neuroimaging features of a small infarct core and a large perfusion-mismatch volume, representing substantial at-risk tissue, within 24 hours after symptom onset or after they were last known to be well. The patients were randomly assigned to undergo endovascular therapy and receive medical management or to receive medical management alone. The primary outcome was an excellent functional outcome (defined by a modified Rankin scale score of 0 [no symptoms] or 1 [no clinically significant disability]) at 90 days.
sections.results: A total of 304 patients underwent randomization, of whom 300 were included in the modified intention-to-treat population: 144 in the endovascular-therapy group and 156 in the medical-management group. At 90 days, a modified Rankin scale score of 0 or 1 was reported in 69.4% of the patients in the endovascular-therapy group and in 50.0% of those in the medical-management group (odds ratio, 2.32; 95% confidence interval, 1.41 to 3.81; P<0.001). Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage within 48 hours occurred in 3 patients in each group. Serious procedure-related complications occurred in 19 patients (13.2%) in the endovascular-therapy group. Among all the participants, one death occurred (in the endovascular-therapy group).
sections.conclusion: In this trial from China involving patients with mild acute ischemic stroke caused by large-vessel occlusion and substantial at-risk tissue on perfusion imaging, endovascular therapy performed within 24 hours after symptom onset plus medical management resulted in better 90-day functional outcomes than medical management alone, without an increase in the risk of symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage but with a high incidence of serious procedural complications. (Funded by Fujian Medical University Union Hospital and others; MILD-MT ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06179017.).

items.title: Mechanical Thrombectomy 24 to 72 Hours after Large-Vessel Ischemic Stroke.

sections.objective: Endovascular thrombectomy is an established treatment for acute ischemic stroke. Whether the benefit extends to patients with salvageable brain tissue in the infarct who present more than 24 hours after symptom onset or the time when they were last known to be well is uncertain.
sections.methods: We conducted an open-label, randomized trial with blinded outcome assessment at comprehensive stroke centers in China. Patients with acute ischemic stroke from large-vessel occlusion of the anterior circulation and imaging-identified salvageable brain tissue at 24 to 72 hours were assigned to receive endovascular therapy plus standard medical care (intervention group) or standard medical care alone (control group). The primary outcome was functional status, defined by the score on the modified Rankin scale (range, 0 to 6, with higher scores indicating greater disability and a score of 6 indicating death) at 90 days, with results assessed as the distribution of scores in each group. Secondary outcomes included disability, neurologic impairment, and safety.
sections.results: A total of 336 patients were included in the intention-to-treat population, with 168 assigned to each group. The median time from symptom onset or from the point when the patient was last known to be well to randomization was 38.5 hours. Endovascular therapy resulted in a more favorable distribution of modified Rankin scale scores at 90 days than standard medical care alone (common odds ratio for a better functional outcome, 1.74; 95% confidence interval, 1.19 to 2.55). Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage occurred in 4.8% of the patients in the intervention group and in no patients in the control group, and the 90-day case fatality rate was 6.0% and 1.8%, respectively.
sections.conclusion: Among patients who presented 24 to 72 hours after an acute ischemic stroke from large-vessel occlusion of the anterior circulation and had imaging-identified salvageable tissue, endovascular therapy resulted in better functional outcomes than standard care but led to a higher risk of intracranial hemorrhage and death. (Funded by the National Health Commission Capacity Building and Continuing Education Center and others; LATE-MT ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05326932.).

items.title: A DNA Typewriter records the cell lineage history of a mouse, from zygote to late organogenesis.
items.abstract: Mammalian biology unfolds over time, within tissues and organs opaque to our eyes and instruments. We applied DNA Typewriter, a sequential molecular recorder, to record the cell lineage of a mouse over nearly 2 weeks of development. From one embryo, we reconstructed a time-calibrated, parsimony-supported, zygote-rooted phylogeny of 1.28 million transcriptionally profiled cells. A burst of editing unequivocally marks the daughters of the first cleavage, which serve as inline replicates. We quantified clonal dominance arising during gastrulation. Tree siblings share cell type far above chance; heterotypic siblings mark terminal differentiations. Temporal sweeps of clade co-occurrence recover a dated hierarchy of cell type couplings; imputed labels for internal nodes recapitulate known state paths. A lineage-anchored ontogeny of mammalian development, long out of reach, is coming into view.

items.title: Aspirin Omission at the Time of Primary Percutaneous Coronary Intervention in STEMI.

sections.objective: The safety of omitting up-front treatment with aspirin during primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) in patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) remains unclear.
sections.methods: We conducted a multicenter, open-label, randomized trial in Japan involving patients with STEMI who were undergoing primary PCI. Patients were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio before PCI to receive low-dose prasugrel monotherapy or dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) with aspirin and low-dose prasugrel for 12 months. The primary outcome was a composite of death from any cause, stroke, or myocardial infarction at 12 months, which was assessed for noninferiority with a prespecified noninferiority margin of 1.50 for the 95% confidence interval of the hazard ratio. The major secondary outcome was major bleeding (defined as a bleeding event of Bleeding Academic Research Consortium [BARC] type 3 [nonfatal major bleeding] or 5 [fatal bleeding]) at 12 months, which was assessed for superiority if noninferiority was established for the primary outcome.
sections.results: A total of 2216 patients were included in the full analysis population; 1109 were assigned to receive monotherapy and 1107 to receive DAPT. At 12 months, death from any cause, stroke, or myocardial infarction had occurred in 124 patients (Kaplan-Meier estimate, 11.0%) in the monotherapy group and in 94 patients (Kaplan-Meier estimate, 8.5%) in the DAPT group (hazard ratio, 1.34; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.02 to 1.75; P = 0.40 for noninferiority). Major bleeding had occurred in 61 patients (Kaplan-Meier estimate, 5.6%) in the monotherapy group and in 92 patients (Kaplan-Meier estimate, 8.4%) in the DAPT group (hazard ratio, 0.66; 95% CI, 0.47 to 0.91). The percentages of patients with definite or probable stent thrombosis and serious adverse events appeared to be similar in the two groups.
sections.conclusion: Among patients with STEMI who were undergoing primary PCI, low-dose prasugrel monotherapy initiated before PCI was not noninferior to DAPT for 12 months with respect to a composite of death from any cause, stroke, or myocardial infarction at 12 months. (Funded by Boston Scientific Japan; PREMIUM ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05709626.).

items.title: Disrupting a cargo receptor entrapment complex is a therapeutic node for distinct proteinopathies.
items.abstract: Toxic accumulation of mutant proteins within the secretory pathway contributes to genetically and clinically distinct proteinopathies, including inherited retinal disease. We identify a cargo receptor entrapment complex whose disruption clears accumulated mutant proteins and ameliorates disease phenotypes in the kidney and eye. The complex comprises transmembrane emp24 domain (TMED)7, TMED2, TMED9, and TMED10, and it retains structurally and functionally diverse mutant proteins in the early secretory pathway through TMED7 binding to the Golgi protein GRASP55. Disrupting this interaction-dependent entrapment mechanism promotes the clearance of accumulated cargoes. In vivo inducible genetic deletion of TMED7 or treatment with the small-molecule BRD7635 reverses histopathological hallmarks and rescues functional deficits across distinct proteinopathies, including mitigation of vision loss in a mouse model of retinitis pigmentosa. Together, these findings reveal a shared mechanism of mutant protein entrapment that can be therapeutically targeted across distinct diseases.

items.title: Lipid-Lowering Strategies in the Era of Early Atherosclerosis Detection: 2026 ACC Scientific Statement: A Report of the American College of Cardiology.
items.abstract: Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) begins early in life, driven in large part by cumulative exposure to low-density lipoprotein cholesterol and other atherogenic lipoproteins. Contemporary evidence from epidemiologic cohorts, genetic studies, imaging studies, and lipid-lowering trials supports a paradigm of earlier identification and more sustained treatment of individuals at increased ASCVD risk. This American College of Cardiology Scientific Statement reviews the rationale for early adoption of lipid-lowering strategies, with emphasis on lifetime lipid burden, inherited and acquired risk enhancers, and the role of subclinical atherosclerosis assessment. Available clinical trial data suggest that greater absolute low-density lipoprotein cholesterol reduction and longer treatment duration can reduce ASCVD events, even though direct evidence remains limited in younger populations at low short-term risk. Atherosclerosis detected by imaging may identify individuals whose ASCVD risk is underestimated by traditional calculators, but optimal strategies for screening, treatment thresholds, safety, adherence, cost-effectiveness, and value require further study. Clinicians should integrate estimated short- and long-term risk, lipid burden, risk enhancers, imaging findings when appropriate, and patient preferences to guide individualized, shared decision making to reduce lifetime ASCVD risk.

items.title: Gender disparities in cataract-related blindness and visual impairment: analysis of data from 204 countries.

sections.objective: Identifying macro-level factors associated with gender disparities in cataract-blindness is crucial for identifying opportunities to reduce vision loss and promote equitable eye care access.
sections.methods: We used country-level data from 204 countries from the Global Burden of Disease-2019, with gender disparity defined as excess females with age-standardised cataract-vision loss (blindness + moderate- and severe visual impairment) compared to males and six country-level socio-developmental indicators. We measured associations using multivariable linear regression models with robust standard errors.
sections.results: Across countries, combined cataract vision loss was 205.73 ± 196.08 per 100,000 population (range: 200.54-836.23) higher in females (Females: 1179.5 ± 792.4 vs Males: 973.8 ± 634.7) After adjusting for confounders, Middle East North Africa region (MENA) had highest gender disparity [Adj.β: 289.4, 95% CI: 190.4-388.2; p < 0.001)]. Female literacy (Adj.β: -20.6, 95% CI: -37.9, -3.3, p < 0.05), total-cataract-blindness (Adj.β: 0.54, 95% CI: 0.41, 0.66, p < 0.001), and per capita health expenditure [low-expenditure: Adj. β: -80.3, 95% CI: -159.4, -1.2; p < 0.05; medium-expenditure: Adj. β: -98.8, 95% CI: -185.8, -11.7; p < 0.05] were associated with gender disparity in cataract-combined vision loss, moderate and severe vision impairment but not with cataract blindness alone. The total burden of cataract blindness (Adj.β: 1.05 [95% CI: 0.77-1.33] was the only factor strongly related to cataract blindness alone.
sections.conclusion: Gender disparities exist in cataract-related vision loss, with variations across regions. Lower literacy rates, lower health expenditures, and a higher burden of cataract-blindness were associated with such disparities.
sections.other: Although cataract blindness declined globally by 32.2% between 1990 and 2019, gender disparities in cataract-related vision loss have persisted, and in some regions, worsened. The highest disparities were observed in South Asia and the Middle East-North Africa region, underscoring regional inequities in access to eye care for women. Macro-level predictors of disparity: Lower female literacy, lower health expenditure per capita, and poorer national development metrics (low HDI, high GII) were strongly associated with higher gender disparities in cataract-related vision loss. Total burden as a key driver: Countries with a higher total burden of cataract blindness also had greater gender disparity, indicating that overwhelmed health systems may disproportionately disadvantage women. Female literacy as a protective factor: Higher female literacy was linked to significantly lower gender disparity in cataract-related vision impairment, reinforcing the critical role of education in improving health equity. Nonlinear effect of health spending: While increased health expenditure initially reduced gender disparities, the benefit plateaued beyond a certain threshold, suggesting that financial inputs alone are insufficient without addressing structural and sociocultural barriers.

items.title: Outcomes of Endovascular Repair for Stanford Type B Aortic Dissection with Concurrent Retrograde Intramural Hematoma Involving the Aortic Arch and/or Ascending Aorta (Zone 0-2) in a Chinese Population: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

sections.objective: To evaluate the outcomes of thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) for type B aortic dissection (TBAD) with concurrent retrograde intramural hematoma (RTIMH) involving the aortic arch, with or without further extension into the ascending aorta.
sections.methods: A systematic search of MEDLINE and EMBASE to June 2026 was performed. Studies reporting TEVAR outcomes in adults with TBAD-associated RTIMH, defined as a primary intimal tear at or distal to Ishimaru zone 3 with retrograde intramural hematoma extension into zones 0-2, were included. Co-primary outcomes were technical success and post-TEVAR retrograde type A aortic dissection (RTAD), defined as the new development of a communicating dissection flap within the previously non-flow intramural hematoma. Secondary outcomes included early mortality, stroke, type I endoleak, reintervention, survival, aortic rupture, and aortic remodelling. Proportions were pooled using single-arm random-effects meta-analysis following logit transformation; remaining findings were synthesised narratively.
sections.results: Seven retrospective cohort studies comprising 342 patients, all from mainland Chinese institutions, were included. The pooled technical success rate was 99% (95% CI 97-99%; I2 = 0.0%). The pooled post-TEVAR RTAD rate was 3% (95% CI 1-8%; I2 = 7.6%), with all events preceded by proximal stent-graft-induced new entry. Secondary outcomes included pooled 30-day mortality of 2% (95% CI 1-4%; I2 = 0.0%), aortic rupture of 2% (95% CI 1-4%; I2 = 0.0%), reintervention of 7% (95% CI 5-11%; I2 = 0.0%), late all-cause mortality of 4% (95% CI 3-6%; I2 = 0.0%), and type I endoleak of 4% (95% CI 2-7%; I2 = 0.0%). All studies reporting pre- and post-procedural imaging demonstrated reductions in ascending aortic diameter and hematoma thickness, with complete ascending IMH resolution in 52.5-100% of patients.
sections.conclusion: TEVAR is technically feasible with low perioperative mortality and consistent aortic remodelling in selected patients with TBAD-associated RTIMH. Post-TEVAR RTAD and type I endoleak represent the principal procedure-specific risks. Contemporary evidence remains limited to small retrospective cohorts from a single geographic region.

items.title: One-Year Outcomes of Surgical Versus Endovascular Revascularization for Acute Limb Ischemia in the SAPLING-ALI Registry.

sections.objective: Despite the increasing use of endovascular therapy as an alternative to surgery for acute limb ischemia, individualized treatment selection remains challenging. We compared outcomes of endovascular therapy versus surgery and sought to identify patient characteristics favoring either strategy.
sections.methods: This multicenter retrospective study included consecutive patients with acute limb ischemia (Rutherford category 1-2b) who underwent revascularization at 13 Japanese institutions between July 2011 and March 2025; patients with thrombosed popliteal artery aneurysm were excluded. The primary outcome was amputation-free survival, defined as freedom from major amputation or death from any cause. The primary analysis was a Cox model adjusted for 13 baseline covariates with hospital as a categorical covariate; propensity score weighting was used as a sensitivity analysis. Subgroup analyses were performed to identify characteristics favoring either strategy.
sections.results: Of 978 patients (endovascular therapy, n = 607; surgery, n = 371), those treated with endovascular therapy more often had diabetes, hemodialysis, dementia, and non-ambulatory status. Unadjusted 1-year amputation-free survival was lower with endovascular therapy than with surgery (68.7% vs 76.3%; log-rank P = .001), but the adjusted hazard ratio for death or major amputation was 1.03 (95% confidence interval, 0.77-1.38; P = .84). Results were consistent with overlap weighting (hazard ratio 1.15; 95% confidence interval, 0.93-1.42) and across other sensitivity analyses. Thirty-day mortality was 13.1% after endovascular therapy and 8.9% after surgery (P = .05), and the difference was attenuated after weighting. No subgroup favoring either strategy was identified (all P for interaction ≥ .18).
sections.conclusion: Unadjusted amputation-free survival was lower after endovascular therapy than after surgery, but the difference disappeared after adjustment for patient characteristics and hospital, and no subgroup favoring either strategy was identified. Endovascular therapy, being less invasive, may be a reasonable alternative to surgery for acute limb ischemia.

items.title: Rhegmatogenous Retinal Detachment: A Contemporary Review of Repair Techniques, Common Complications, Advances in Imaging and Access to Care.
items.abstract: Rhegmatogenous retinal detachment (RRD) is a vision-threatening ophthalmic emergency with a rising global incidence driven by aging populations and the worldwide myopia epidemic. Despite modern surgical techniques achieving anatomic reattachment in over 90% of cases, as many as 40% of successfully reattached eyes fail to recover functional vision, underscoring a persistent and clinically important gap between anatomic and visual outcomes. We synthesize contemporary evidence across a wide clinical spectrum of RRD. We examine the pathophysiologic cascade initiated by posterior vitreous detachment, the classification and clinical significance of types of retinal breaks, and the epidemiologic burden of established risk factors including high myopia, pseudophakia, and hereditary vitreoretinal disorders. The historical evolution of repair techniques is reviewed. Evidence based rationale for personalized surgical selection in phakic, pseudophakic, and giant retinal tear-associated detachments is then discussed. The most common complications of surgical repair are addressed, with particular emphasis on proliferative vitreoretinopathy as the dominant cause of surgical failure and the most pressing unmet therapeutic need. We further examine how neighborhood-level social determinants of health independently shape presentation severity and visual recovery, underscoring that equitable access to timely care can be as fundamental to influencing outcomes as surgical technique itself. Finally, emerging pharmacologic strategies, intraoperative optical coherence tomography, robotic surgical assistance, and imaging prognostic tools, with and without the use of artificial intelligence are evaluated as future directions. Advancing outcomes in RRD will require the integration of surgical refinement, emerging pharmacology, imaging-based prognostication, and an unwavering commitment to equitable access across all patient populations.

items.title: Network Meta-Analysis of Complement Inhibitors for Geographic Atrophy in Age-Related Macular Degeneration.
items.abstract: Pegcetacoplan (PEG) and avacincaptad pegol (ACP) are approved complement inhibitors for geographic atrophy (GA) secondary to age-related macular degeneration, yet direct comparative evidence is lacking. We conducted a PROSPERO-registered frequentist network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials of complement inhibitors for GA. MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched through November 5, 2025. Twenty-two reports of 13 trials (5,126 patients) were included. Compared with sham, moderate-certainty evidence showed that PEG 15 mg monthly and every other month reduced untransformed GA lesion growth. ACP estimates were imprecise when reconstructed from arm-level data, but both ACP doses reduced GA growth when the trials' model-based treatment differences were used, consistent with the pivotal trials. No ACP and PEG regimens differed in GA growth, and no complement inhibitor improved low-luminance visual acuity. At final follow-up, PEG regimens and ACP 4 mg increased neovascular age-related macular degeneration compared with sham, and its incidence was lower with ACP 2 mg than with PEG 15 mg monthly in indirect comparison (low certainty), with no other ACP and PEG difference. These comparisons are limited by differences in trial populations, endpoints, and follow-up. Head-to-head trials with functional endpoints are needed.

items.title: Secondary analysis of the FIELD randomized trial evaluated the performance of GFR slope in a non-glomerular model of estimated GFR decline.

sections.objective: Glomerular Filtration Rate (GFR) decline is a recent surrogate kidney endpoint for trials. Estimated GFR (eGFR) decline has been modelled using GFR slope, correlating total and chronic GFR slopes with composite kidney endpoints. Several included interventions caused an initial eGFR decline mediated by glomerular hemodynamics. We tested the association of GFR slopes with clinical endpoints for fenofibrate, an agent with an acute, non-glomerular eGFR decline (i.e. no effect on inulin clearance).
sections.methods: The FIELD trial randomized adults to fenofibrate or placebo. Total slope was calculated using a repeated measures 2-slope linear mixed model for the entire intervention period. A three-year sensitivity analysis was performed. Chronic slope was calculated from month four. The composite kidney endpoint was doubling of serum creatinine or 40% decline/eGFR under 15 ml/min/1.73 m2/kidney death/kidney replacement therapy. The total slope from baseline to eight-week washout eGFR was an exploratory subgroup analysis.
sections.results: 9795 participants were followed for five years. Post-washout eGFR was ascertained in 660 sub-study participants. Fenofibrate produced an acute eGFR decline of -9.05 ml/min/1.73 m2. Fenofibrate improved chronic slope (significant between-group difference 0.61 ml/min/1.73 m2/ annum [95% CI 0.50 to 0.71]) but worsened total slope (significant between group difference -1.54, 95% CI -1.65 to -1.44). Fenofibrate significantly increased the clinical endpoint (hazard ratio 1.48, 95% CI 1.16 to 1.89). Washout analyses demonstrated treatment benefit on total slope, contrary to on-study analyses in the overall cohort.
sections.conclusion: Conventional composite endpoints include surrogate components that may not always accord with measured kidney function, though widely accepted in trials. Total slope and the conventional composite yielded concordant treatment effects under an acute eGFR change both larger and mechanistically distinct from those in previous validation work, supporting the conclusion that total slope will produce similar results to conventional endpoints.

items.title: Dietary sodium restriction enhances the renoprotective efficacy of endothelin-A receptor antagonism in proteinuric chronic kidney disease.

sections.objective: Endothelin-A receptor antagonists (ERAs) are emerging as an important treatment for proteinuric chronic kidney disease (CKD). As with renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS) inhibition, dietary sodium intake may influence their therapeutic efficacy, but this has not been investigated. Here, we examined whether dietary sodium restriction enhances the systemic and kidney effects of acute selective endothelin-A (ETA) receptor antagonism in proteinuric CKD.
sections.methods: In a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover study, 12 adults (mean age 46 years) with non-diabetic proteinuric CKD (mean eGFR 55 mL/min/1.73 m2; median proteinuria 1.8 g/day) receiving maximally tolerated RAAS inhibition completed two 14-day dietary interventions (habitual dietary sodium intake [13.3 g salt/day] and dietary sodium restriction [6.3 g salt/day, approximating guideline-recommended levels]) in random order. During each dietary period, participants underwent two study visits and received intravenous infusion of either placebo or the selective ET A receptor antagonist, BQ123. Systemic hemodynamics, arterial stiffness, kidney hemodynamics and proteinuria were assessed following each intervention.
sections.results: BQ123 produced comparable reductions in systolic blood pressure (about 12-14 mmHg), systemic vascular resistance and arterial stiffness under both dietary conditions and increased kidney blood flow (about 320-335 mL/min) irrespective of dietary sodium intake. In contrast, significant reductions in glomerular filtration rate (peak placebo-adjusted reduction: about 5 mL/min/1.73 m2), effective filtration fraction (peak reduction about 1.5%), and proteinuria (about 300 μg/min) were observed only during dietary sodium restriction and not during habitual sodium intake.
sections.conclusion: Dietary sodium restriction enhances the short-term kidney efficacy of selective endothelin-A receptor antagonism in proteinuric CKD while preserving its beneficial systemic hemodynamic effects. As ERAs become established therapies for proteinuric kidney disease, these findings suggest that adherence to dietary sodium restriction may maximize their kidney-protective benefits. Whether the acute changes demonstrated here translate into long-term kidney protection requires prospective evaluation.

items.title: Bedside ECMO Cannulation by Intensivists and Emergency Physicians.
items.abstract: The number of centers capable of initiating extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) for critically ill patients with refractory cardiac or respiratory failure is expanding. Historically, patients were taken to the operating room or catheterization laboratory for ECMO cannulation by cardiothoracic surgeons and perfusionists. More recently, non-surgeons who have undergone specialized training are performing percutaneous ECMO cannulation and initiation of support at the bedside at some centers. This approach is attractive, in part, because of the timely initiation of ECMO and avoidance of the risk of patient deterioration during transport to a procedural area. The purpose of this article is to provide a roadmap for intensivists and emergency physicians to lead ECMO bedside procedures including veno-venous (VV), veno-arterial (VA), and hybrid veno-arteriovenous (V-AV) cannulation at ECMO-capable centers. These procedures demand cognitive and technical skills that are already foundational to critical care practice, including vascular access guided by point-of-care ultrasound and leadership during a dynamic resuscitation. A team-based approach to bedside ECMO cannulation is presented and illustrated with figures and video, including preparation, procedural execution, subsequent patient management, and programmatic considerations such as training and credentialing requirements.

items.title: Checkpoint Inhibition during primary hepatitis E virus infection alters memory development of virus-specific T-cells in humans.

sections.objective: HEV infection is an underappreciated differential diagnosis in patients presenting with acute hepatitis during immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy. As T-cells are the key targets of ICIs, particularly through blockade of inhibitory immune checkpoints such as PD-1, this intervention is likely to influence the dynamics and differentiation fate of de novo primed virus-specific T-cells during primary HEV infection. We therefore aimed to examine how PD-1 blockade during primary HEV-infection influences expansion, contraction, and memory formation of virus-specific CD8+ T-cells.
sections.methods: HEV-specific CD8 and CD4+ T-cells were analyzed by applying a reverse phenotyping approach combined with single-cell transcriptomics and TCR sequencing, as well as multiparameter flow cytometry with MHC class I tetramers. We characterized HEV-specific T-cell responses in patients receiving ICI and in untreated patients during acute-viremic infection and after viral clearance.
sections.results: Under ICI, de novo primed HEV-specific CD8+ T-cells showed enhanced clonal expansion, cytotoxicity, and terminal differentiation. Rather than transitioning into classical memory subsets, these cells retained a cytotoxic transcriptional program and acquired features of long-lived effector-like T-cells (LLEC). While HEV-specific T-cells remained detectable over > 2 years, their functional recall responsiveness declined in ICI-treated patients.
sections.conclusion: Collectively, our findings demonstrate that PD-1 blockade during the formation of a primary immune response reshapes the fate of the antiviral CD8+ T-cell pool, favoring terminally differentiated effector states over conventional memory formation, with potential implications for viral infections, vaccination, and immunotherapeutic strategies.
sections.other: Our study represents the first demonstration in a human model that PD-1 blockade during primary antigen exposure reshapes antiviral CD8+ T-cell effector formation and memory differentiation. By identifying PD-1 signaling during a primary immune response as a regulator of antiviral CD8+ T-cell fate, our findings establish a conceptual framework for understanding how immune checkpoint blockade influences the development of primary antiviral T-cell responses, with implications for viral infections, vaccination, and immunotherapeutic strategies.

items.title: Smoke, Not Smoking, as a Possible Risk Factor Triggering Conversion in Leber's Hereditary Optic Neuropathy: A Retrospective Case Series.

sections.objective: To describe the association of wildfire smoke exposure with conversion of Leber hereditary optic neuropathy (LHON) mutation carriers to symptomatic LHON.
sections.methods: In this retrospective observational case series, we performed an exploratory analysis of our institutional LHON registry for patients under observation during 2017-2018. We described four LHON mutation carriers who developed bilateral vision loss within 4-8 weeks of documented wildfire smoke exposure during the 2017 Wine Country and 2018 Camp (Paradise) fires in Northern California. We performed an exploratory analysis of our institutional LHON registry for patients under observation during 2017-2018.
sections.results: All four carriers resided in regions where the Air Quality Index exceeded 150 for multiple consecutive days. Two individuals had remained asymptomatic carriers for more than four decades prior to conversion. In the registry cohort of 40 carriers, 15 converted during 2017-2018. Conversion occurred in 7 of 9 carriers (78%) residing in the Northern California wildfire-affected region, compared with 8 of 31 (26%) residing elsewhere (odds ratio 10.1; Fisher's exact p=0.02). In a time-window analysis restricted to the 8 weeks following the November 2018 Paradise fire, 3 of 5 Northern California carriers at risk (60%) converted compared with 0 of 23 carriers residing outside the region (odds ratio 65.8; Fisher's exact p=0.006).
sections.conclusion: We observed temporal clustering of LHON conversion following wildfire smoke exposure and regional enrichment of conversion during 2017-2018. Although causality cannot be established in this retrospective analysis, acute particulate exposure may represent a mitochondrial stressor that lowers the threshold for conversion in susceptible individuals.
sections.other: Four genetically confirmed LHON mutation carriers who developed bilateral vision loss after the 2017 Wine Country, or 2018 Camp Fire (Paradise) wildfire and 40 genetically confirmed carriers were examined and followed up from 2017-2018 to 2026. Time from regional wildfire smoke exposure to symptomatic conversion and conversion frequency among registry carriers.

items.title: Historical Redlining and Present-Day Vision Disability in Atlanta, Georgia: The Mediating Role of Neighborhood Deprivation.

sections.objective: To investigate whether present-day vision disability (VD) prevalence reflects historical redlining in Atlanta, Georgia, quantify mediation by neighborhood deprivation, and assess generalizability across redlined United States (U.S.) cities.
sections.methods: Ecologic, cross-sectional, retrospective analysis. Census tract-level VD prevalence (2015-2019 American Community Survey) was linked to Home Owners' Loan Corporation (HOLC) grade, Social Deprivation Index (SDI), and distance to nearest eye care office. Unadjusted associations used Spearman correlations and Wilcoxon rank-sum tests. Besag-York-Mollié 2 (BYM2) spatial models estimated risk ratios (RR) per 1-SD adjusting for age and sex; causal mediation analysis quantified the indirect effect of HOLC grade on VD through SDI. Analyses were repeated across 108 cities and pooled via random-effects meta-analysis. Statistical significance was defined as p<0.05 for correlation and group comparison tests, and 95% confidence intervals for BYM2 model and mediation analysis estimates.
sections.results: In Atlanta, HOLC score was not associated with VD risk (fully adjusted RR=0.89, 95% CI: 0.72-1.09). The indirect effect through SDI was significant (ACME=1.15 percentage points per one-grade increase, 95% CI: 0.76-1.56, p<0.001), and the direct effect was not (ADE=0.11 percentage points, 95% CI: -0.60-0.66, p=0.88); the proportion mediated through SDI was 91%. Lack of vehicle access was most strongly associated with VD risk (RR=1.73, 95% CI: 1.39-2.12). Eye care office distance did not differ by HOLC grade (p=0.56). Nationally, the HOLC-VD association (pooled RR=1.21, 95% CI: 1.18-1.24) attenuated after SDI adjustment (pooled RR=1.03, 95% CI: 1.01-1.05); 78% was mediated through SDI (pooled ACME=0.37 percentage points, 95% CI: 0.33-0.41). The indirect effect varied substantially between cities (I²=65.3%).
sections.conclusion: In Atlanta and across redlined U.S. cities, the association between redlining and VD prevalence was largely explained by neighborhood deprivation. Lack of transportation access was most strongly associated with VD, and eye care offices in Atlanta were not farther from more redlined neighborhoods, suggesting access and affordability may underlie these inequities. Reducing place-based VD inequities may require investing in social determinants, such as transportation, beyond clinical services.
sections.other: 93 Atlanta census tracts and 12,432 tracts across 108 redlined U.S. cities. VD prevalence by HOLC grade, SDI, racial composition, and eye care distance.

items.title: Sarcoidosis for the Dermatologist : Part 2: Treatment and Monitoring.
items.abstract: Sarcoidosis is a multisystem inflammatory disease that may require treatment for multiorgan disease, or organ specific involvement, including sometimes for primary cutaneous disease or cutaneous involvement that fails to respond to treatment for multiorgan disease. Skin treatments range from local therapy to systemic anti-inflammatory, immunomodulatory, and immunosuppressive agents, depending on the extent and severity of involvement. Management is individualized and aims to control disease activity, prevent irreversible organ damage, reduce treatment-related toxicity, and improve quality of life. Because the clinical course is variable, careful follow-up is essential, with attention to treatment response, relapse, and the development of extracutaneous involvement. Ongoing monitoring should be guided by symptoms, organ involvement, and the therapies being used.

items.title: Reflectance Confocal Microscopy Improves Clinicopathologic Correlation in Facial Lentigo Maligna: A Prospective Real-Life Study.

sections.objective: Pigmented facial lesions pose a diagnostic challenge, and lentigo maligna (LM) must not be overlooked as a differential diagnosis. Despite integrated evaluation with clinical examination and dermoscopy, diagnostic uncertainty may persist. Reflectance confocal microscopy (RCM) has emerged as a complementary diagnostic tool. To assess the diagnostic performance of RCM in clinically suspected cases of facial LM.
sections.methods: We conducted a prospective single-center study between February 2021 and September 2025, including 248 flat pigmented facial lesions clinically suspected of LM. RCM was performed, and lesions suggestive of LM were biopsied. Results were compared with the gold standard, defined as the diagnosis obtained after integrated clinical-dermoscopic-RCM-histopathological evaluation.
sections.results: RCM achieved 100% sensitivity and 94.2% specificity for LM diagnosis, and 75% (n = 187) of lesions did not undergo biopsy following RCM evaluation. Perifollicular dendritic cells on RCM were present in 100% of biopsy-proven LM. Among all LM, 20% had an initially negative biopsy despite RCM findings suggestive of LM, prompting additional histopathological evaluation that ultimately confirmed LM in all cases.
sections.conclusion: RCM strengthens the correlation between clinical, dermoscopic, and histopathologic findings in LM.
sections.other: Single-center real-world study, limited to facial lesions, potential underestimation of false negatives and operator-dependent interpretation.

items.title: Efficacy and safety of anti-IL-4Rα stapokibart for adults with moderate-to-severe prurigo nodularis: results from a phase 3 randomized trial.

sections.objective: Prurigo nodularis (PN) is a chronic inflammatory skin disease with limited treatment options. To evaluate the efficacy and safety of anti-IL-4Rα stapokibart in adults with moderate-to-severe PN.
sections.methods: This was a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 study (NCT06424470) conducted in 39 centers in China between June 24, 2024, and April 14, 2025. Eligible patients who had a diagnosis of PN for ≥3 months were randomly assigned 1:1 to receive subcutaneous stapokibart 300 mg (a loading dose, 600 mg) or placebo every 2 weeks for 24 weeks.
sections.results: Totally 200 patients were enrolled (n=100 per group). At week 24, significantly greater proportions of stapokibart-treated patients versus placebo achieved ≥4-point improvement in Worst Itch Numeric Rating Scale (64.0% vs. 33.0%; primary endpoint) and Investigator's Global Assessment for chronic nodular prurigo stage score of 0/1 (45.0% vs. 14.0%; key secondary endpoint) (both P<0.0001). Benefits were also observed in patients' quality of life, skin pain, sleep disturbance, and anxiety/depression. The incidence of treatment-emergent adverse events was similar between the stapokibart and placebo groups (79.0% vs. 73.0%).
sections.conclusion: 24 weeks of treatment with stapokibart demonstrated high efficacy and favorable safety in adults with moderate-to-severe PN.
sections.other: Chinese patients only.

items.title: Endovenous Microwave Versus Radiofrequency Ablation for Isolated Small Saphenous Vein Reflux: A Randomised Controlled Trial.

sections.objective: No randomised trial has directly compared endovenous microwave ablation (EMA) with radiofrequency ablation (RFA) for isolated small saphenous vein (SSV) reflux. This trial aimed to determine whether EMA is non-inferior to RFA for 12-month SSV trunk occlusion and to characterise the sural nerve injury profile of each modality.
sections.methods: Patients with duplex-confirmed symptomatic isolated SSV reflux were randomised 1:1 to EMA or RFA at a single vascular centre. The primary efficacy endpoint was duplex-confirmed SSV trunk occlusion at 12 months, assessed in the per-protocol (PP) population with a pre-specified 10% non-inferiority margin. The key secondary safety endpoint was clinically confirmed sural nerve injury at 12 months. Patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) - Venous Clinical Severity Score (VCSS), Aberdeen Varicose Vein Questionnaire (AVVQ), and Chronic Venous Insufficiency Questionnaire (CIVIQ-14) - were assessed longitudinally using a mixed-effects model for repeated measures (MMRM).
sections.results: Baseline characteristics were well balanced between groups. At 12 months, the PP occlusion rate was 98.4% in both groups (EMA 60/61; RFA 62/63; risk difference -0.05%, 95% CI -4.6% to 4.5%), confirming non-inferiority (P < .001). The intention-to-treat sensitivity analysis (EMA 92.3%, RFA 95.4%) also satisfied the 10% margin. Clinically confirmed sural nerve injury occurred in 3.3% (2/61) of EMA patients and 1.6% (1/63) of RFA patients (P = .614); all sensory symptoms resolved within six months. EMA was associated with a nominally shorter operative time (30.2 ± 9.0 vs 33.1 ± 7.9 min; P = .054) and a nominally lower one-month VCSS score (P = .030); neither difference persisted beyond three months. MMRM analysis showed significant within-group improvement across all three PROM instruments over 12 months (all P < .001), with no significant between-group difference at any timepoint.
sections.conclusion: With adequate perivenous tumescent anaesthesia and a proximal-selective dual-cycle ablation strategy, EMA achieves 12-month SSV occlusion non-inferior to RFA. Sural nerve injury rates are low and reversible with both modalities. EMA offers a marginal operative time advantage and may confer early symptomatic benefit, though these differences are not sustained at 12 months. Both techniques appear to be appropriate first-line options for symptomatic isolated SSV reflux.

items.title: The neural mechanisms of fast versus slow decision-making.
items.abstract: One hallmark of intelligent behavior is the ability to optimize how much time is devoted to decisions. Yet the principles governing decision timing remain unclear. Here, we developed a novel paradigm for directly comparing decision-making between mice and humans. This approach allowed us to combine widefield and 2-photon imaging in the mouse frontal cortex with optogenetic inhibition to examine the underlying mechanisms. We found that history-dependent refinement of sequences in the medial frontal cortex (MFC), versus a thresholding mechanism in the lateral frontal cortex (LFC), provides a unified logic for decision strategy on a trial-by-trial basis. Notably, behavioral performance and strategy were profoundly disrupted by optogenetic inhibition of the MFC compared with that of the LFC, revealing a dominant cognitive role for MFC in decision selection and timing. These dynamics reflect reinforcement-learning updates that explain timing variability better than sensory evidence. Our findings provide a computational framework that unifies voluntary decision-making across species.

items.title: Low-Concentration Atropine Eye Drops in Children With Myopia and Intermittent Exotropia: The AMIXT2 Randomized Clinical Trial.

sections.objective: The optimal atropine concentration for myopia control in children with coexisting intermittent exotropia (IXT) remains uncertain. To compare the efficacy and safety of 0.01%, 0.02%, and 0.04% atropine eye drops in children with myopia and IXT.
sections.methods: This single-center, double-masked, 3-arm randomized clinical trial was conducted from September 2023 to March 2026. Children aged 6 to 12 years with basic-type IXT and myopia (cycloplegic spherical equivalent [SE], -0.50 to -6.00 diopters [D]) were enrolled. Data analysis was conducted from March 2026 to July 2026. Participants were randomized 1:1:1 to 0.01%, 0.02%, or 0.04% atropine eye drops nightly in both eyes.
sections.results: Among 264 randomized children (mean [SD] age, 8.4 [1.5] years; 130 female [49.2%]), 224 (84.8%) completed the 12-month assessment. Mean (SD) SE changes were -0.43 (0.50) D, -0.35 (0.51) D, and -0.18 (0.60) D with 0.01%, 0.02%, and 0.04% atropine, respectively (overall P = .001). Compared with 0.01% and 0.02% atropine, 0.04% atropine was associated with less SE progression (vs 0.01%: difference, 0.24 D; 95% CI, 0.11-0.37 D; P < .001; vs 0.02%: difference, 0.16 D; 95% CI, 0.04-0.29 D; P = .02). Mean (SD) AL changes were 0.31 (0.25) mm, 0.25 (0.23) mm, and 0.15 (0.29) mm, respectively (overall P < .001); corresponding differences for 0.04% vs 0.01% and 0.02% were -0.16 mm (95% CI, -0.22 to -0.10 mm; P < .001) and -0.10 mm (95% CI, -0.16 to -0.04 mm; P < .001). Mean (SD) near exodeviation decreased by 3.46 (5.76) prism diopters (PD), 4.84 (8.05) PD, and 6.13 (7.11) PD, respectively (overall P = .04); the reduction was greater with 0.04% vs 0.01% atropine (difference, -2.68 PD; 95% CI, -4.78 to -0.57 PD; P = .008). Study drug-related photophobia occurred in 8 (9.1%), 9 (10.2%), and 19 participants (21.6%) in the 0.01%, 0.02%, and 0.04% atropine groups, respectively; no participant discontinued treatment because of photophobia.
sections.conclusion: In the AMIXT2 randomized clinical trial among children with myopia and IXT, 0.04% atropine eye drops were associated with less myopia progression and axial elongation over 12 months than 0.01% or 0.02% atropine eye drops. Higher concentrations were associated with greater reductions in near magnitude of exodeviation, which warrant further investigation.
sections.other: The primary outcome was 12-month change in cycloplegic SE. Secondary outcomes included changes in axial length (AL), exotropia conditions, binocular vision, and ocular safety parameters.

items.title: Grafting vs Intraoperative Mitomycin C for Preventing Pterygium Recurrence: A Randomized Clinical Trial.

sections.objective: Postoperative recurrence remains a major challenge after primary pterygium surgery, and whether grafting approaches are more effective than intraoperative mitomycin C (MMC) in reducing recurrence remains uncertain. To determine whether grafting with conjunctival autograft (CAG) or amniotic membrane transplant (AMT) is superior to MMC in preventing 1-year recurrence after primary pterygium excision.
sections.methods: This multicenter, open-label randomized clinical trial with masked outcome assessment with 12-month follow-up was conducted at 5 tertiary hospitals in China. Enrollment and follow-up occurred between January 2016 and December 2020, and data were analyzed from September 2025 through January 2026. Patients aged 18 to 80 years with primary pterygium were enrolled and randomly assigned 1:1:1 to AMT (n = 249), MMC (n = 248), or CAG (n = 253). Standardized pterygium excision with conjunctival excision extending radially 4 mm from the limbus, combined with AMT, MMC, or CAG.
sections.results: Of 750 randomized participants (mean [SD] age, 57.2 [10.5] years; 487 women [64.9%]), 681 (90.8%) completed follow-up. Recurrence in the intention-to-treat analysis was 57 participants of 249 with AMT (22.9%), 34 of 248 with MMC (13.7%), and 13 of 253 with CAG (5.0%). Risk differences were 9.2 percentage points for AMT vs MMC (98.33% CI, 0.6-17.9; P = .01), 17.9 for AMT vs CAG (98.33% CI, 10.5-25.4; P < .001), and 8.7 for MMC vs CAG (98.33% CI, 2.2-15.2; P = .001). Risk ratios were 1.69 (98.33% CI, 0.99-2.91; P = .02), 4.62 (98.33% CI, 2.14-9.97; P < .001), and 2.73 (98.33% CI, 1.20-6.20; P = .004), respectively. Complete-case analyses yielded similar results. Adverse events occurred in 18 of 249 AMT participants (7.2%), 28 of 248 MMC participants (11.3%), and 16 of 253 CAG participants (6.3%), with no intervention-related serious adverse events.
sections.conclusion: In this randomized clinical trial, among patients undergoing primary pterygium excision, recurrence was lowest with CAG, intermediate with MMC, and highest with AMT. The moderate magnitude of the between-procedure differences makes recurrence prevention an important-but not exclusive-determinant of surgical choice and may inform individualized surgical management.
sections.other: The primary outcome was 12-month postoperative recurrence. Secondary outcomes included best-corrected visual acuity, epithelial healing time, and conjunctival congestion scores.

items.title: Three-Year Outcomes of Endovascular Therapy Using Covered Stent-Grafts Versus Interwoven Nitinol Stents in Severely Calcified Femoropopliteal Artery Disease From a Retrospective Multicenter Registry.

sections.objective: This study aimed to compare the long-term safety and efficacy of Viabahn covered stent-grafts (CSG) and Supera peripheral stents (SPS) in calcified femoropopliteal artery lesions.
sections.methods: We retrospectively analyzed 341 cases who had Rutherford class 2 to 6 peripheral artery disease and underwent endovascular therapy (EVT) with either CSG (n = 137) or SPS (n = 204) for femoropopliteal lesions with bilateral calcification assessed by fluoroscopic image based on Peripheral Arterial Calcium Scoring System classification, between April 2017 and February 2021 at 7 cardiovascular centers in our country.
sections.results: Following propensity score (PS) matching, the final study population comprised 142 matched patients with no remarkable intergroup difference in baseline characteristics. The 3-year primary patency was 70.9% in the CSG group and 56.2% in the SPS group, respectively, and was not statistically different (P = .083). Moreover, no significant difference was noted in freedom from target lesion revascularization (72.8% vs 63.5%, P = .16), limb salvage rate (100.0% vs 96.2%, P = .32), and overall survival rate (67.6% vs 66.6%, P = .61). Stratification analysis revealed that advanced age and current smoking had a significant interaction on the association of CSG versus SPS implantation with restenosis (interaction P < .05).
sections.conclusion: In patients with severely calcified femoropopliteal lesions, the 3-year primary patency was not significantly different between EVT using CSG and SPS following PS matching.Clinical ImpactSevere calcification in femoropopliteal disease remains a challenge for EVT. Covered stent-graft and SPS are reliable devices for calcified femoropopliteal lesions. We compared the 3-year outcomes in patients undergoing EVT using either CSG or SPS. Following the propensity matching, the 3-year primary patency was not different at 70.0% and 56.2% (P = .083) in the CSG (n = 71) and SPS (n = 71) groups, respectively. Moreover, no significant difference was noted in freedom from target lesion revascularization and limb salvage rate.

items.title: Endovascular Recanalization of Chronically Occluded Femoropopliteal Bypass Grafts: Feasibility and Early Clinical Outcomes.

sections.objective: Chronic occlusion of femoropopliteal bypass grafts remains a complex clinical challenge, particularly in patients with peripheral arterial disease (PAD) who have limited surgical options and high operative risk. Although redo bypass surgery has traditionally been considered the standard treatment, it is associated with increased morbidity. Advances in endovascular techniques have expanded revascularization strategies; however, data on graft-directed endovascular recanalization remain limited.
sections.methods: This retrospective single-center study included 32 consecutive patients who underwent endovascular recanalization for chronically occluded femoropopliteal bypass grafts between January 2018 and December 2024. A stepwise graft-directed technique was applied, consisting of intraluminal guidewire crossing, sequential balloon predilatation, and stent implantation along the graft body and anastomotic segments when necessary. Technical success, procedural safety, and changes in ankle-brachial index (ABI) were evaluated.
sections.results: The mean age of the patients was 69.8 ± 9.6 years, and 68.8% were male. Technical success was achieved in 30 patients (93.8%). Median ABI improved significantly from 0.34 (interquartile range [IQR]: 0.22-0.48) before intervention to 0.71 (IQR: 0.58-0.84) after revascularization. Stent implantation was performed in all patients, with a median of 3 stents per case. Periprocedural complications occurred in 2 patients (6.3%) and were managed conservatively or by endovascular means. No procedure-related mortality or major limb loss was observed during hospitalization.
